newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds trade down in line with market caution.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds trade down in line with market caution.

text.p: Irish bond prices were marked down in thin trading on Wednesday in line with general market reaction to a stronger-than-expected retail sales report from the U.S., dealers said.
"We're underperforming by a couple of basis points in shorts in particular," one dealer said. "In the 10-year bond most markets have fallen, yields are higher, and we're trading in line with bunds."
Most markets had traded down in response to U.S. data showing a rise in sales in February of 0.8 percent, dealers said, a number that was 0.2 percent above Wall Street forecasts.
"The strength of that number will have increased concerns that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) may tighten credit at its next meeting on March 25," a dealer said.
The FOMC meeting, at which interest rate policy will be decided, remains a major focus for bond markets.
Dealers said next week's auction of 10-year bonds was also having a dampening effect on the Irish market.
Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency is due next Tuesday to auction 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent bond due 2006.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 23.5 pence from Tuesday's close to 101.72 to yield 6.05 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 43 pence from the close at 109.02 to yield 6.67 percent.
Elsewhere, the U.S. bond market remained nervous about inflation despite the Federal Reserve's Beige Book on Wednesday describing price pressures as "temperate".
UK gilts remained weak, eyeing a volatile performance from T-bonds following the retail sales data.
